I'm going with the assumption that since the fat kid in your story is in high school, he's at least 14. Most 14-year-olds have a part-time job (or at least me & all my friends did when I was 14) so I'm assuming he has his own money which he can use to buy food. Another argument could be, "but his parents made him fat when he was young, maybe he doesn't know how to lose the weight." Which again, I'm going to have to call bullshit on. This is the information age - everything anyone could ever want to know is at our fingertips via the internet. If this kid wanted to lose weight, he could look online and start learning about CICO, use something like MyFitnessPal to count calories, and websites like T-Nation to learn about lifting. Heck, even YouTube has videos on how to perform certain exercises, and they've got videos on how to prepare healthy meals, too. At 14 you might not be completely independent of your parents (you likely still live on them and rely on them for things like transport) but I think your mental capacity is enough that you are responsible for what you put in your mouth, how much (if any) exercise you do, and whether or not you stay/become fat.

Where's the age cut-off? I'm not sure. But I can tell you it's definitely before 14.
